title: Edit in place
intro: A `StringBuilder` is one object whose characters you edit in place: `append`, `insert`, `delete`, `reverse` and `setLength` change its buffer, and there is nothing to catch. Predict the buffer after each call.

rounds.right: Three calls, one object: `sb` never moved, its buffer just changed. It prints {result}.

rightEach.append: `append` adds to the end of the buffer.
rightEach.insert: `insert(2, ...)` slides everything from index 2 along to make room.
rightEach.reverse: `reverse()` turns the buffer itself back to front.

why.append.front: `append` adds to the end; `insert(0, ...)` is the one that adds to the front.
why.append.same: A `StringBuilder` changes itself: `append` edits the buffer, so there is no new object to catch.
why.insert.after: `insert(2, ...)` puts the new text at index 2, so it lands in front of the character that was at index 2.
why.insert.end: `insert` puts the text at the index you give it, not at the end.
why.reverse.same: Unlike a String method, `reverse()` changes the builder itself: no catching needed.

rounds.right: `delete(start, end)` leaves out its end index, just like `substring`, and `setLength` keeps the first characters. It prints {result}.

rightEach.delete: `delete(1, 3)` removes indexes 1 and 2: the end index is left out.

why.delete.inclusive: The end index is left out: `delete(1, 3)` removes indexes 1 and 2, and the character at index 3 stays.
why.delete.shifted: `delete(1, 3)` starts at index 1, the second character: indexes count from 0.
why.setLength.one: `setLength(3)` keeps three characters, the ones at indexes 0, 1 and 2.
why.setLength.tail: `setLength` keeps the start of the buffer and cuts off the end.

rounds.right: `insert(1, "t")` puts the `t` at index 1, and everything from there slides one box along.

why.insert.after: `{chosen}` puts the `t` at index 2: it makes {got}.
why.insert.before: `{chosen}` puts the `t` at index 0, in front of everything: it makes {got}.

rounds.right: `setLength(4)` keeps the first four characters and drops the rest.

why.setLength.more: `{chosen}` keeps five characters: all of them, so nothing changes.
why.setLength.less: `{chosen}` keeps only three characters: it makes {got}.
